messages:
maya (support): FYI we're getting multiple customer escalations for eu2-hosted API: widespread 502/504s and long tail streaming timeouts starting ~10:12 UTC. Customer logs show socket resets and streaming stalls.

ben (eng-oncall): I'm looking. Can you paste sample request ids / customer timestamps?

maya (support): Sample request id: req_0x9a7f3, customer timestamp 2026-03-17T10:12:14Z. Support-bot posted alert cluster: eu2-ingress high 502-rate.

support-bot: [alert] eu2-hosted: 502-rate spike (10m) -> 12.6x baseline.

carol (netops): Seeing increased packet loss on our eu2-az3 <-> eu2-az1 links and some cross-AZ RTT spikes. Pulling BGP and interface counters now.

alice (sre): Correlating with backend errors: gateway returned 502 when connection to runtime timed out after 10s. Logs show a lot of backend connection resets.

ben (eng-oncall): Can you run a quick mtr from edge-to-runtime in eu2 to verify path? Also grep k8s proxy logs for conn reset reasons.

carol (netops): Pasted MTR (truncated):
```
Start: 10:18:03
HOST: edge-eu2 -> runtime-eu2
 1 10.0.1.1 0.2% 1ms
 2 100.64.2.5 0.0% 2ms
 3 198.51.100.9 12.3% 18ms  <-- packet loss here
 4 203.0.113.22 11.9% 22ms
 5 203.0.113.30 0.0% 23ms
```
Loss and jitter concentrated starting at the transit hop (ASN 64512).

carol (netops): BGP update stream shows intermittent withdraws for transit-peer ASN64512 at 10:13:XX and 10:15:YY. Provider reported flaps on carrier link.

ben (eng-oncall): That matches the customer repro window. We're seeing degraded KV cache connections and increased tail latencies — likely due to packet loss causing TCP retransmit timeouts.

jim (customer-success): Customer A is on a high-throughput hosted endpoint and sees streaming disconnects; they're asking for ETA. They're asking if we can fail traffic to eu1.

alice (sre): Short mitigation: 1) enable route failover to eu1 for affected customers (manual for now), 2) temporarily reduce keepalive timeouts and increase connection retries on gateway, 3) enable fallback model variant with smaller token footprint to reduce per-request sockets.

ben (eng-oncall): I'm pushing a routing policy to shift 20% of new sessions to eu1 for non-data-residency customers and enable higher retry budget for streaming. Doing canary now.

ben (eng-oncall): Patch applied: route-policy eu2->eu1 canary=20%. Observability: 502-rate down ~60% for canary cohort.

maya (support): Noted. I've told Customer A we have a partial mitigation and we're doing provider escalation. They're still worried about billing credits if this persists.

carol (netops): Opened ticket with TransitPeer-3 / ASN64512 (ticket #TP-8841). Provider ACK'd flaps and is investigating a physical interface flap causing microbursts. ETA unknown.

alice (sre): For triage we need to collect: tcpdump from ingress proxies (pcap for 10:10-10:25), connection metrics (SYN/FIN/RST), and a trace of affected request ids. I started collection job:
```
kubectl -n hosted-inference exec -it proxy-abc -- tcpdump -w /tmp/eu2-10-10-25.pcap port 443
```
Saved artifacts to /artifacts/incidents/eu2/4529991234/.

ben (eng-oncall): Also check infra-metrics: CPU, socket pool exhaustion. So far CPU normal, but ephemeral socket count spike. Adding soft-limit increase to proxy threadpool to reduce immediate 502s.

infra-bot: incident artifact uploaded: /artifacts/incidents/eu2/4529991234/eu2-pcap.pcap (s3://redwood-incidents).

carol (netops): Provider updates: they observed high CRC errors on trunk and are RFOing maintenance to replace optics on fiber. Expected window 30-90 mins.

ben (eng-oncall): Operational decision: keep canary at 20% and increase to 40% if customer impact persists. Rolling update to routing config done.

maya (support): Customers notified with status page link and recommended mitigation steps (retry/backoff guidance). Customer A requested credits; escalated to billing with incident reference.

jim (customer-success): Notifying top-affected customers directly. Collecting business impact for credit requests.

alice (sre): Postmortem checklist: capture provider ticket, pcap, k8s proxy logs, gateway metrics, and routing decisions. We'll want to add automated cross-AZ reroute playbook to reduce manual steps.

ben (eng-oncall): Temporary runbook notes:
- If eu2 502-rate > 5x baseline AND provider reports transit-flap -> enable route-policy failover to eu1 for non-residency customers.
- Increase proxy retry budget and reduce keepalive timeout to 5s for new connections.
- Notify CS/billing and open provider ticket.

maya (support): Closing loop: provider replaced optics, link stabilized at 11:08 UTC, we saw packet loss drop and 502 rates returned to baseline by 11:12. Customers confirmed resumed normal ops.

ben (eng-oncall): Leaving this thread open for postmortem doc. Assigning to alice for lead on writeup.

alice (sre): Taking lead. I'll start draft and tag infra/netops. Will include recommended automation.

maya (support): Thanks all. :thumbsup:
